parsed.explanation: Parent national framework applies directly with no island variation. Documented positives are only climate signals: same-sex unions registrable and performed for visitors since 2012, and a general anti-discrimination law said to cover visitors, without text naming gender identity, markers or facilities. No traveller-facing trans exposure is documented, but screening, documents, facilities, custody, care, violence, police response and minors are all undocumented. In this thin dossier silence is not safety, and marriage/anti-discrimination law cannot be credited as a trans-specific protection. Extrapolating from the non-criminalising, functioning parent framework suggests no organised targeting, yet unanswered traveller questions keep it below documented reduced-risk cases.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower: 0.65-C documents lawful expression, foreign-document acceptance, community role and a court remedy. This dossier documents none of those trans-specifically, only marriage and general anti-discrimination climate.

Similar to slightly higher: 0.55-A has documented recurring service refusals despite protections. This dossier has no documented recurring harm, but also no documented trans protections, so it cannot sit materially above.
Higher: 0.35-A has a documented universal birth-sex facility rule with courts rejecting complaints. No such universal exposure, targeting or failed remedy is documented here.

parsed.synthesis: Combined regime is the parent framework operating directly, with no additional island layer. Its documented 2012 visitor marriage registration and general anti-discrimination coverage indicate functioning, non-criminalising institutions as a climate signal, but provide no operative trans traveller protection for borders, facilities, custody or care. With every primary axis undocumented, the rating extrapolates cautiously from that parent structure rather than treating silence as safety, placing it in upper elevated risk below documented reduced-risk acceptance-plus-remedy cases.
